references.text: Moses reminds the people that they were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord brought them out with a strong hand, the same reminder of slavery as the background for the commandment.
God introduces the Ten Commandments by reminding Israel that he brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
The Israelites are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; therefore they must not be sold as slaves.
Parallel text where Israel is reminded of slavery in Egypt as the basis for the Sabbath commandment.
The same exhortation to remember slavery in Egypt as motivation for keeping the commandments.
Reminder that Israel was a slave in Egypt and that the Lord redeemed them, as the foundation for treating others justly.
Repetition of the reminder about slavery in Egypt as motivation to show mercy.
The Lord redeemed Israel from the house of bondage and from Pharaoh's hand, the same theme of deliverance from Egypt.
Christ gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness, a New Testament echo of God's redemption of Israel.
Believers are redeemed with Christ's precious blood, which connects to God's redemption of Israel from Egypt.
